setup: Back flat against a smooth wall
Walk your feet out about two foot-lengths
execution: Slide down until your thighs are level
Press your back into the wall
faults: Don't push on your thighs with your hands
Don't let your knees drift in

notes: Use a wall with a non-slip floor and shoes with grip so your feet don't slide.
A long hard hold can raise blood pressure. Keep breathing throughout, and stand up if you feel lightheaded.
Pick a depth you can hold with good form; a higher sit is easier.
If pain lingers or comes back, stop this exercise and get it checked by a physio or doctor.
stopIf: Pain at the knee that builds during the hold

regressions.name: Higher wall sit
regressions.reason: Knees bent less, so the thighs work less.

regressions.name: Shorter holds
regressions.reason: Several short holds with rests build up to one long one.

progressions.name: Single-leg wall sit
progressions.reason: One foot lifted puts all the work on the other leg.

progressions.name: Wall sit with a ball squeeze
progressions.reason: Squeezing a ball between the knees adds inner-thigh work.

substitutions.name: Bodyweight squat
substitutions.reason: Same muscles through a full range instead of a hold.

substitutions.name: Leg extension
substitutions.reason: Quad work on a stack that is easy to load.

guideBrief.cameraNote: Side view at hip height, figure facing right with the wall on the left. Shows the hip and knee at right angles and the back flat on the wall. A still hold, so the animation slides down once, holds, and slides up.

keyPositions.label: Start
keyPositions.describe: Standing with the back against the wall, feet about two foot-lengths in front of it, hip-width apart.

keyPositions.label: Hold
keyPositions.describe: Back flat on the wall, thighs level with the floor, knees over the ankles, shins vertical. Hands resting by the sides or crossed on the chest, not on the thighs.

ikHints: Back and head in contact with the wall throughout
